title: The Office - Out Of Control Spending

segments.en: Hello, everyone, and welcome to EnglishPod.
So, Marco, how are you doing today?
segments.zh: 那么，马可，你今天过得怎么样？

segments.en: I'm really happy to be back, ready to deliver another great podcast for all our listeners.
segments.zh: 我真的很高兴回来，准备为我们所有的听众提供另一个很棒的播客。

segments.en: And we've got an intermediate lesson today about spending money.
segments.zh: 我们今天有一个关于花钱的中级课程。

segments.en: Yeah, specifically spending money in a company.
segments.zh: 是的，特别是在一家公司花钱。

segments.en: We're going to be listening to a business meeting as a company describes how they're spending money.
segments.zh: 我们将收听一场商务会议，会上公司在讲述他们是怎么花钱的。

segments.en: And they're actually looking at their profit and loss statement.
segments.zh: 他们实际上正在查看他们的损益表。

segments.en: Well, Marco, can you tell us a little bit about a profit and loss statement?
segments.zh: 好吧，Marco，你能告诉我们一些关于损益表的信息吗？

segments.en: Well, all companies come out with a profit and loss statement every year or every three months.
segments.zh: 好吧，所有公司每年或每三个月都会出一个损益表。

segments.en: And it's basically a document that shows all the money that the company is spending and all the money that the company is earning.
segments.zh: 它基本上是一份文件，显示了公司花费的所有钱以及公司所赚取的所有钱。

segments.en: So it's a document that outlines how much money the company makes and how much it spends.
segments.zh: 所以它是一份文件，概述了公司赚了多少钱和花了多少钱。

segments.en: So in the end, basically, it'll tell you we're making money or we're losing money.
segments.zh: 所以最终，它会告诉你我们正在赚钱，或者我们正在亏钱。

segments.en: So we're going to be listening to some people discuss a profit and loss statement in just a moment.
segments.zh: 所以稍后我们就会听到几个人讨论损益表。

segments.en: But before we do that, it's time for vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 但在我们这样做之前，是时候进行词汇预览了。

segments.en: So today on our vocabulary preview, we have two words for you.
segments.zh: 所以今天在我们的词汇预览中有两个词要讲。

segments.en: So let's take a look at the first one.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看第一个。

segments.en: So expenses are things that you have to spend money on regularly.
segments.zh: 所以费用是你必须定期花钱的事情。

segments.en: So for example, in a company, regular company expenses are salaries or office supplies or the phone bills, internet bills.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，在公司中，公司的常规费用是工资或办公用品或电话账单、互联网账单。

segments.en: Maybe in a household or a family, your expenses might be your food, perhaps your transportation or your rent or your heating bill.
segments.zh: 也许在家庭或家庭中，您的费用可能是您的食物，也许是您的交通、租金或取暖费。

segments.en: So these are all things you spend money on regularly.
segments.zh: 所以这些都是你经常花钱的东西。

segments.en: Let's take a look at our second word.
segments.zh: 让我们来看看我们的第二个词。

segments.en: So when something is through the roof, it's...
segments.zh: 所以当某样东西是 through the roof 时，它就是...

segments.en: So for example, we can talk about gas prices are through the roof lately.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，我们最近可以谈论汽油价格。

segments.en: Gas prices have gone really high in the past couple of months.
segments.zh: 在过去的几个月里，汽油价格真的很高。

segments.en: So when we talk about through the roof, it means that the number is really high.
segments.zh: 所以我们说 through the roof，就是指这个数字真的很高。

segments.en: We typically use this word with numbers.
segments.zh: 我们通常将这个词与数字一起使用。

segments.en: It also gives you the idea that the number has risen really quickly.
segments.zh: 它还让您认为这个数字很快就上升了。
所以是 through the roof——高得离谱。

segments.en: All right, Marco, do you think it's time for the dialogue?
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，你认为是时候进行对话了吗？

segments.en: Yep, let's listen to the dialogue.
As always, the first dialogue is going to be a little bit fast, so it might be a little bit difficult, but...
segments.zh: 与往常一样，第一次对话会有点快，所以可能有点困难，但是...

segments.en: Don't worry if you don't understand everything, because we will explain all of the key language in a minute.
segments.zh: 如果您不了解所有内容，请不要担心，因为我们将在一分钟内解释所有关键语言。

segments.en: Okay, so now the last point on our agenda.
segments.zh: 好了，现在来看议程的最后一项。

segments.en: Jill, let's go over the profit and loss statement.
segments.zh: 吉尔，让我们回顾一下损益表。

segments.en: Well, the main issue here, as you can see, is that our expenses are through the roof.
segments.zh: 正如你所见，主要问题是我们的开支高得离谱。

segments.en: These numbers are off the charts.
segments.zh: 这些数字简直高得吓人。

segments.en: Well, sir, the company expenditures on entertainment and travel are out of control.
segments.zh: 好吧，先生，公司在娱乐和旅行方面的支出已经失控。

segments.en: Look at these bills, for example.
Just this month, we've paid over $20,000 for hotel charges.
segments.zh: 就在本月，我们已经支付了超过 20,000 美元的酒店费用。

segments.en: The list goes on and on.
Here, this is a bill for $5,000 for spa treatment.
segments.zh: 这儿有张五千美元的水疗账单。

segments.en: $5,000 were expensed in one night at a place called Wild Things?
segments.zh: 在一家叫“Wild Things”的地方，一晚上竟报销了五千美元？

segments.en: Thank you for your very thorough analysis.
segments.zh: 谢谢你分析得这么详细。

segments.en: Okay, so this accountant, she's pretty thorough, hey?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这位会计师，她很彻底，嘿？

segments.en: She's really persistent about her job, and the manager apparently is a little bit embarrassed.
segments.zh: 她真的很坚持自己的工作，经理显然有点尴尬。

segments.en: I wonder why that could be.
segments.zh: 我想知道为什么会这样。

segments.en: Well, we'll talk about that in a little while.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们稍后会讨论这个问题。

segments.en: Why don't we take a look at our language takeaway for today?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不看看我们今天的语言要点？

segments.en: In today's language takeaway, we're going to look at three words, and the first word is expenditures.
segments.zh: 在今天的语言要点中，我们将看三个词，第一个词是支出。

segments.en: So expenditures sounds pretty close to expenses, right?
segments.zh: 所以支出听起来很接近费用，对吧？

segments.en: It's pretty similar, but it has a little bit of a difference.
segments.zh: 它非常相似，但它有一点区别。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to some examples and see if we can understand?
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不听一些例子，看看我们是否能理解呢？

segments.en: If elected president, I will increase expenditures on health and education by 12%.
segments.zh: 如果当选总统，我将在健康和教育方面的支出增加 12%。

segments.en: We really need to control our travel expenditures.
segments.zh: 我们真的需要控制我们的旅行支出。

segments.en: From now on, all managers will fly economy class.
segments.zh: 从现在开始，所有经理都将乘坐经济舱。

segments.en: Because of the rise in oil prices, expenditures on food are higher than they have ever been.
segments.zh: 由于油价上涨，食品支出比以往任何时候都要高。

segments.en: So expenditures is the total amount of money that you're spending on something.
segments.zh: 所以支出是你花在某物上的总金额。

segments.en: That's the total amount of money versus expenses is the things that you spend money on.
segments.zh: 也就是说，expenditures 是花钱的总金额，而 expenses 是你花钱买的具体东西。

segments.en: Our next word is out of control.
segments.zh: 我们下一个词是 out of control（失控）。

segments.en: So when something is out of control, it's crazy.
segments.zh: 所以当某事失控时，这太疯狂了。

segments.en: Now, let's take a look at our last word for today.
segments.zh: 现在，让我们来看看我们今天的最后一个词。

segments.en: So go over is a pretty simple word.
segments.zh: 所以 Go Over 是一个非常简单的词。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to some examples so we can understand go over?
segments.zh: 我们不如先听几个例子，来理解 go over 的意思？

segments.en: I need to go over this report one last time to make sure there are no mistakes.
segments.zh: 我需要最后一次复习这份报告，以确保没有错误。

segments.en: Can you help me go over my presentation?
segments.zh: 你能帮我复习一下我的演示文稿吗？

segments.en: I want to make sure it's perfect.
Let's go over these numbers one more time and make sure there are no mistakes.
segments.zh: 让我们再回顾一下这些数字，并确保没有错误。

segments.en: Yeah, this is a really common word and it basically means look at carefully.
segments.zh: 是的，这是一个非常常见的词，它基本上意味着仔细看。
是的，或者说是复习、回顾。

segments.en: In English, we often find simple little words, they fit together really well.
segments.zh: 在英语中，我们经常找到简单的小词，它们非常适合。

segments.en: And you think, oh, they're so easy, like the word go over, so easy.
segments.zh: 你会想，哦，它们太简单了，比如 go over 这个词，多简单啊。

segments.en: But it's the way that they interact with each other that makes them...
segments.zh: 但正是他们之间的互动方式才使他们...

segments.en: Or it makes you sound much better.
segments.zh: 或者它让你听起来更好。

segments.en: So go over, in this case, we might say, let's go over the lesson.
segments.zh: 所以，这种情况下我们可以说，let's go over the lesson。

segments.en: Yeah, and that's a more natural way of saying something like that.
segments.zh: 是的，这是一种更自然的说法。

segments.en: Okay, so we've taken a look at our language takeaways for today.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们今天看看我们的语言要点。

segments.zh: 我认为是时候再听一次对话了。

segments.zh: 而这一次，对话会更慢，所以我们可以理解和倾听我们刚刚谈到的所有单词。

segments.zh: 好了，现在来看议程的最后一项。

segments.en: Jill, let's go over the profit and loss statement.
segments.zh: 吉尔，让我们回顾一下损益表。

segments.en: Well, the main issue here, as you can see, is that our expenses are through the roof.
segments.zh: 正如你所见，主要问题是我们的开支高得离谱。

segments.en: These numbers are off the charts.
segments.zh: 这些数字简直高得吓人。

segments.en: Well, um, sir, the company expenditures on entertainment and travel are out of control.

Just this month, we've paid over $20,000 for hotel charges.

Here, this is a bill for $5,000 for spa treatments.
segments.zh: 在这里，这是一张 5,000 美元的水疗护理账单。

segments.en: $5,000 were expensed in one night at a place called Wild Things?
segments.zh: 在一家叫“Wild Things”的地方，一晚上竟报销了五千美元？

segments.en: Thank you for your very thorough analysis.
segments.zh: 谢谢你分析得这么详细。

segments.en: Yeah, and you know, I heard a lot of really great phrases in this dialogue that I'd like to look at now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 是的，你知道，我在这个对话中听到了很多非常棒的短语，我现在想在流利表达中看到。

segments.zh: 所以今天在流利表达上，我们为您准备了三个词。

segments.en: Let's start by looking at the first one, off the charts.
segments.zh: 让我们从图表上看第一个。

segments.en: So this word is very similar to through the roof.
segments.zh: 所以这个词和 through the roof 非常相似。

segments.en: So let's listen to some examples of how we can use off the charts in a different situation.
segments.zh: 所以让我们听几个例子，看看 off the charts 在不同的情况下怎么用。

segments.en: Oil prices have gone up and our costs are off the charts.
segments.zh: 油价上涨，我们的成本高得离谱。

segments.en: Your sales are off the charts this year.
segments.zh: 今年你的销售额高得离谱。

segments.en: Our losses are off the charts.
So Marco, do you think I can change off the charts for through the roof in these examples?
segments.zh: 那么 Marco，你觉得我能把这些例子里的 off the charts 换成 through the roof 吗？

segments.en: You can use off the charts or through the roof.
segments.zh: 你可以用 off the charts，也可以用 through the roof。

segments.en: Both of them mean the same thing.
segments.zh: 两者的意思都是一样的。

segments.en: So two ways of saying really, really, really high.
segments.zh: 所以有两种说法真的，真的，真的很高。

segments.en: But they're very commonly used in a business setting.
segments.zh: 但它们非常常用于商业环境。

segments.en: So this next word is a phrase that you can use if you want to tell somebody that you'll check something or you'll investigate something.
segments.zh: 所以下一个单词是一个短语，如果你想告诉别人你会检查某事或者你会调查某事，你可以使用它。

segments.en: And we heard it in our dialogue.
segments.zh: 我们在对话中听到了它。

segments.en: So let's listen to the clip.

segments.zh: 这意味着我会检查一些东西。
是的，我会看看发生了什么。

segments.en: Does it mean you're going to take action?
segments.zh: 这是否意味着你要采取行动？

segments.en: So I think we've got another word that does mean you're going to take action.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们还有另一个词，它确实意味着你要采取行动。

segments.en: So this word means that you're going to do something about it.
segments.zh: 所以这个词意味着你要做点什么。

segments.en: So I will do something about it.
I will investigate and I'll do it.

segments.zh: 我会做一个非常彻底的分析。

segments.en: Marco, I guess one of the benefits of being an executive in a company, especially a large company, is you get a lot of amazing benefits.
segments.zh: Marco，我猜在尤其是大公司当高管的福利之一，就是能享受很多很棒的待遇。

segments.en: When you are a manager or a CEO of one of these big companies, you get a lot of great things like, I don't know, a private jet maybe.
segments.zh: 当您是这些大公司之一的经理或首席执行官时，您会得到很多很棒的东西，例如，我不知道，可能是私人飞机。

segments.en: Or the company often pays for your house.
segments.zh: 或者公司经常为你的房子买单。

segments.en: Or for your car, they'll give you a company car.
segments.zh: 或者为了你的车，他们会给你一辆公司的车。

segments.en: They'll pay for your kids' or your children's tuition for high school.
segments.zh: 他们将支付您孩子或您孩子的高中学费。

segments.en: Also, I've heard about entertainment bonuses.
segments.zh: 另外，我听说过娱乐奖金。

segments.zh: 所以你可以去餐厅吃饭，拿上收据，回公司报销。

segments.zh: 这些是一些巨大的好处，对吧？

segments.zh: 所以马可，我很想知道我们的听众的开支是多少。

segments.en: We definitely want to know what crazy expenses you have.
segments.zh: 我们绝对想知道你有什么疯狂的开支。

segments.en: My spending on Coke Zero has gone through the roof since we started this podcast.
segments.zh: 自从我们开始做这个播客，我花在零度可乐上的钱就一路飙升。

segments.zh: 你每周花在零度可乐上的钱可不少，对吧？
